J.2 Proof of Lemma 3.2

Proof.

Let f⁡(θ):=LDPO​(θ,𝒟~)f(\theta):=L_{\mathrm{DPO}}(\theta;\tilde{\mathcal{D}}) and θ⋆:=θ^=arg⁡minθ⁡f⁡(θ)\theta^{\star}:=\hat{\theta}=\arg\min_{\theta}f(\theta). Since ff is μ\mu-strongly convex and differentiable, see Lemma E.14 (Nika et al., 2025), its gradient is μ\mu-strongly monotone: for all θ\theta,

⟨∇f​(θ)−∇f​(θ⋆),θ−θ⋆⟩≥μ​‖θ−θ⋆‖22.\langle\nabla f(\theta)-\nabla f(\theta^{\star}),\,\theta-\theta^{\star}\rangle\geq\mu\|\theta-\theta^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}.

Because θ⋆\theta^{\star} minimizes ff, we have ∇f​(θ⋆)=0\nabla f(\theta^{\star})=0. Thus,

μ​‖θ−θ⋆‖22≤⟨∇f​(θ),θ−θ⋆⟩≤‖∇f​(θ)‖2​‖θ−θ⋆‖2,\mu\|\theta-\theta^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\langle\nabla f(\theta),\,\theta-\theta^{\star}\rangle\leq\|\nabla f(\theta)\|_{2}\,\|\theta-\theta^{\star}\|_{2},

where the last inequality is Cauchy–Schwarz.

If θ≠θ⋆\theta\neq\theta^{\star}, dividing both sides by μ​‖θ−θ⋆‖2\mu\|\theta-\theta^{\star}\|_{2} yields ‖θ−θ⋆‖2≤‖∇f​(θ)‖2/μ\|\theta-\theta^{\star}\|_{2}\leq\|\nabla f(\theta)\|_{2}/\mu, and the inequality is trivial when θ=θ⋆\theta=\theta^{\star}.

Taking θ=θ†\theta=\theta^{\dagger} and using (4) together with (5) gives (6). Finally, Lemma E.5 of (Nika et al., 2025) shows that for log-linear policies, if ‖θ^​(x)−θ†‖2≤ϵ/(2​d)\|\hat{\theta}(x)-\theta^{\dagger}\|_{2}\leq\epsilon/(2\sqrt{d}), then ‖πθ^​(x)−πθ†‖1≤ϵ\|\pi_{\hat{\theta}(x)}-\pi_{\theta^{\dagger}}\|_{1}\leq\epsilon. Combining this with (6) yields the stated sufficient condition ε≤μ​ϵ/(2​d)\varepsilon\leq\mu\,\epsilon/(2\sqrt{d}). ∎

J.3 Proof of Theorem 3.4

Proof.

Recall that we assume that the feature embedding is uniformly bounded, e.g.,

‖ψ⁡(s,a)‖2≤1.\|\psi(s,a)\|_{2}\leq 1.

Under this assumption, each feature difference satisfies

‖Δ​ψi‖2=‖ψ⁡(si,ai)−ψ⁡(si,ai′)‖2≤2,\|\Delta\psi_{i}\|_{2}=\|\psi(s_{i},a_{i})-\psi(s_{i},a_{i}^{\prime})\|_{2}\leq 2,

and hence each individual flip contribution is bounded as

‖oi​β​Δ​ψi‖2=β​‖Δ​ψi‖2≤2​β.\|o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\|_{2}=\beta\|\Delta\psi_{i}\|_{2}\leq 2\beta.
Exact attack.

In the exact attack setting, the constraint reads g†=∑i∈ℱoi​β​Δ​ψig^{\dagger}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}o_{i}\beta\,\Delta\psi_{i}. Taking norms and applying the triangle inequality, we obtain

‖g†‖2=‖∑i∈ℱoi​β​Δ​ψi‖2≤∑i∈ℱ‖oi​β​Δ​ψi‖2≤∑i∈ℱ2​β=2​β​|ℱ|.\begin{split}\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}=\left\|\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\right\|_{2}\leq\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}\|o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\|_{2}\leq\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}2\beta=2\beta|\mathcal{F}|.\end{split} (19)

Consequently,

|ℱ|≥‖g†‖2​β.|\mathcal{F}|\geq\frac{\|g^{\dagger}\|}{2\beta}. (20)
Approximate attack.

In the approximate case, we allow that ‖g†+∑i∈ℱoi​β​Δ​ψi‖2≤ε\left\|g^{\dagger}+\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\right\|_{2}\leq\varepsilon. Applying the reverse triangle inequality to the summation term, we have

‖∑i∈ℱoi​β​Δ​ψi‖2≥‖g†‖2−ε.\left\|\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\right\|_{2}\geq\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon.

On the other hand, as in (19), we also have

‖∑i∈ℱoi​β​Δ​ψi‖2≤2​β​|ℱ|.\left\|\sum_{i\in\mathcal{F}}o_{i}\beta\Delta\psi_{i}\right\|_{2}\leq 2\beta|\mathcal{F}|.

Combining these inequalities yields

‖g†‖2−ε≤2​β​|ℱ|,\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon\leq 2\beta|\mathcal{F}|,

so that

|ℱ|≥‖g†‖2−ε2​β.|\mathcal{F}|\geq\frac{\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon}{2\beta}. (21)

∎

J.4 Proof of Lemma 4.1

The proof is a local-improvement argument: if some coefficient were ≥2\geq 2, reducing it by one decreases the penalty by at least 3​M23M^{2}, while the residual term can increase by at most O⁡(B​‖r‖)+O⁡(B2)O(B\|r\|)+O(B^{2}); choosing MM large ensures the penalty decrease dominates, contradicting optimality.

Proof.

‖y⁡(xopt)‖22≤‖y⁡(x⋆)‖22=‖V​x⋆+g†‖22+M2​‖x⋆‖22≤R2+M2​K⋆.\|y(x^{\mathrm{opt}})\|_{2}^{2}\leq\|y(x^{\star})\|_{2}^{2}=\|Vx^{\star}+g^{\dagger}\|_{2}^{2}+M^{2}\|x^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}\leq R^{2}+M^{2}K^{\star}. (22)

Let

r:=V​xopt+g†∈ℝd.r:=Vx^{\mathrm{opt}}+g^{\dagger}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}.

Then from (22) and ‖y⁡(xopt)‖22=‖r‖22+M2​‖xopt‖22≥‖r‖22\|y(x^{\mathrm{opt}})\|_{2}^{2}=\|r\|_{2}^{2}+M^{2}\|x^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{2}^{2}\geq\|r\|_{2}^{2}, we get

‖r‖2≤R2+M2​K⋆.\|r\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{R^{2}+M^{2}K^{\star}}. (23)

We now show that for MM large enough, xoptx^{\mathrm{opt}} cannot have any coordinate with magnitude at least 22. Step 1 (bound the change in the top term). Compute

so

|‖r‖22−‖r~‖22|≤2​‖r‖2​‖vj‖2+‖vj‖22.\bigl|\|r\|_{2}^{2}-\|\tilde{r}\|_{2}^{2}\bigr|\leq 2\|r\|_{2}\|v_{j}\|_{2}+\|v_{j}\|_{2}^{2}.

Since x⋆x^{\star} is feasible, FM​(x⋆)=M2​K⋆F_{M}(x^{\star})=M^{2}K^{\star}. Consider any x∈{0,1}nx\in\{0,1\}^{n}. If 𝟏⊤​x≥K⋆\mathbf{1}^{\top}x\geq K^{\star}, then FM​(x)≥M2​ 1⊤​x≥M2​K⋆=FM​(x⋆)F_{M}(x)\geq M^{2}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}x\geq M^{2}K^{\star}=F_{M}(x^{\star}).

J.7 Proof of Proposition E.1

Proof.

Fix any M>0M>0. Choose any dimension d≥1d\geq 1 and any n≥1n\geq 1. Let g†∈ℝdg^{\dagger}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} be any nonzero vector with

‖g†‖2=M2<M.\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}\;=\;\frac{M}{2}\;<\;M.

Construct V∈ℝd×nV\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n} whose first column is

v1:=−g†,v_{1}:=-g^{\dagger},

and whose remaining columns are arbitrary.

Then the exact flip attack is feasible with the binary vector x⋆=e1∈{0,1}nx^{\star}=e_{1}\in\{0,1\}^{n}:

V​x⋆=v1=−g†,Vx^{\star}\;=\;v_{1}\;=\;-g^{\dagger},

so the optimal flip count is K⋆=‖x⋆‖0=1K^{\star}=\|x^{\star}\|_{0}=1.

Now consider the surrogate objective FM​(x)=‖V​x+g†‖22+M2​ 1⊤​xF_{M}(x)=\|Vx+g^{\dagger}\|_{2}^{2}+M^{2}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}x over x∈{0,1}nx\in\{0,1\}^{n}. For the zero vector,

FM​(0)=‖g†‖22=M24.F_{M}(0)\;=\;\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}^{2}\;=\;\frac{M^{2}}{4}.

For any x≠0x\neq 0 with x∈{0,1}nx\in\{0,1\}^{n}, we have 𝟏⊤​x≥1\mathbf{1}^{\top}x\geq 1, hence

FM​(x)=‖V​x+g†‖22+M2​ 1⊤​x≥ 0+M2>M24=FM​(0).F_{M}(x)\;=\;\|Vx+g^{\dagger}\|_{2}^{2}+M^{2}\,\mathbf{1}^{\top}x\;\geq\;0+M^{2}\;>\;\frac{M^{2}}{4}\;=\;F_{M}(0).

Therefore, the unique minimizer of minx∈{0,1}n⁡FM​(x)\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n}}F_{M}(x) is x^=0\hat{x}=0.

Finally, since g†≠0g^{\dagger}\neq 0, x^=0\hat{x}=0 is infeasible for the exact attack constraint V​x+g†=0Vx+g^{\dagger}=0 (it yields residual ‖g†‖2>0\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}>0), whereas a feasible exact solution exists with one flip. This shows that for the fixed MM we constructed an instance where minimizing FMF_{M} fails to recover a feasible minimum-flip exact attack. Since M>0M>0 was arbitrary, no universal choice of MM can guarantee minimum-flip recovery for all instances. ∎

J.10 Proof of Theorem 5.4

Proof.

We prove impossibility by upper bounding the largest gradient shift ‖V​x‖2\|Vx\|_{2} achievable with at most KK flips, and comparing it to the amount of shift needed to reach tolerance ε\varepsilon.

Suppose there exists a binary vector x∈{0,1}nx\in\{0,1\}^{n} with ‖x‖0≤K\|x\|_{0}\leq K such that ‖V​x+g†‖2≤ε\|Vx+g^{\dagger}\|_{2}\leq\varepsilon. Let r:=V​x+g†r:=Vx+g^{\dagger}. By the reverse triangle inequality,

‖V​x‖2≥‖g†‖2−‖r‖2≥‖g†‖2−ε.\|Vx\|_{2}\;\geq\;\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\|r\|_{2}\;\geq\;\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon. (28)

Thus any successful KK-flip attack must produce a shift of size at least ‖g†‖2−ε\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon.

Spectral norm impossibility (17).

Since xx is binary with at most KK ones, we have ‖x‖2=‖x‖0≤K\|x\|_{2}=\sqrt{\|x\|_{0}}\leq\sqrt{K}. Therefore,

‖V​x‖2≤‖V‖2​‖x‖2≤‖V‖2​K.\|Vx\|_{2}\leq\|V\|_{2}\,\|x\|_{2}\leq\|V\|_{2}\sqrt{K}.

Combining with (28) yields

‖g†‖2−ε≤‖V‖2​K,\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon\leq\|V\|_{2}\sqrt{K},

which contradicts (17).

Coherence impossibility (18).

Let S:=supp⁡(x)S:=\mathrm{supp}(x) so that |S|=‖x‖0≤K|S|=\|x\|_{0}\leq K and V​x=∑i∈SviVx=\sum_{i\in S}v_{i}. Write vi=ai​uiv_{i}=a_{i}u_{i} with ai=‖vi‖2a_{i}=\|v_{i}\|_{2} and ‖ui‖2=1\|u_{i}\|_{2}=1. Expanding the squared norm and using |⟨ui,uj⟩|≤μ⁡(V)|\langle u_{i},u_{j}\rangle|\leq\mu(V) gives

‖V​x‖22=⟨∑i∈Sai​ui,∑j∈Saj​uj⟩=∑i∈Sai2+∑i,j∈Si≠jai​aj​⟨ui,uj⟩≤∑i∈Sai2+μ⁡(V)​∑i,j∈Si≠jai​aj≤|S|​B2+μ⁡(V)|S|(|S|−1)​B2≤B2​(K+μ⁡(V)​K​(K−1)).\begin{split}\|Vx\|_{2}^{2}&=\Big\langle\sum_{i\in S}a_{i}u_{i},\ \sum_{j\in S}a_{j}u_{j}\Big\rangle=\sum_{i\in S}a_{i}^{2}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j\in S\\ i\neq j\end{subarray}}a_{i}a_{j}\langle u_{i},u_{j}\rangle\\ &\leq\sum_{i\in S}a_{i}^{2}+\mu(V)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j\in S\\ i\neq j\end{subarray}}a_{i}a_{j}\leq|S|B^{2}+\mu(V)\,|S|(|S|-1)B^{2}\leq B^{2}\Bigl(K+\mu(V)\,K(K-1)\Bigr).\end{split} (29)

Together with (28), this implies

(‖g†‖2−ε)2≤B2​(K+μ⁡(V)​K​(K−1)),\bigl(\|g^{\dagger}\|_{2}-\varepsilon\bigr)^{2}\leq B^{2}\Bigl(K+\mu(V)\,K(K-1)\Bigr),

which contradicts (18). This completes the proof. ∎
